title: Honest question: has anyone here had a bot beat just holding the index for 6+ months, live, after costs?
author: pigeon_shit
selftext:
Not trolling, genuinely asking. I run a bunch of rule-based paper bots where the rules are locked before day one and every bot is scored daily after costs, losers kept. Most of them fail, which is kind of the point.



So: if you've had one that held up for months after fees and slippage, what did it take, and how did you convince yourself it wasn't luck? And if yours flopped, what was the moment you realized it? Not selling anything, no links. Just trying to learn how people actually separate edge from noise.

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body: I have my own bot in the crypto market, and we’ve now had four consecutive months in the green. So, it is possible though I’m not sure what the situation is like in other markets. I know the crypto space well, which is perhaps why it was easier for me to build something here that performs effectively.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
months after fees, no, not one I'd swear by. what killed most of mine was regime: a rule that looked great through a trending stretch, then bled slowly through chop. I stopped trusting anything that hadn't lived through at least one ugly month.

Quantradin, which I built to run rules like yours on paper against real fills, has the same problem, a few months of paper says very little.
quantradin.com

what's your bar for calling it edge, trade count or calendar time?

comments.author: Upper-Worker8516
comments.body: Everyone one reddit has a dam profitable bot....must be the place high net worth individuals meet....who would have thought it....reddit.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I haven't run one live myself, so I can only say how I'd judge it. Locking rules before day one and keeping the losers is the right setup, since it lets you count how many bots you tried. The way I'd separate edge from noise is to compare each survivor with random entries on the same days and see if it still wins after the count of tries is taken into account. Then I'd check it keeps working in the months after you picked it. Cymetica's Backtest Labs has a fee setting and a held out stretch of data for that kind of check.

comments.author: drguid
comments.body:
Beating the S&P and Nasdaq since I added my AI models to my existing swing trading system.

If the market crashes now then we will soar past the indexes because we're 50% cash. The bot just doesn't fancy the current market much.

Only 2 losing months in 24 months.

comments.author: perp_systems_tinker
comments.body: Very few bots do over 6+ months live after costs. To separate edge from luck, run many random-entry bots on the same data and see how far the best one beats the index. Your best survivor has to clear that, not just the index. Then freeze its rules and judge it only on data after the freeze.
